critical_issues.description: Hardcoded relative path 'static/index.html' will fail if test is run from a different working directory; should use Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'static' / 'index.html' or a configurable base path.
Hardcoded relative path 'static/css/style.css' vulnerable to same working directory issue; should use absolute path resolution relative to test file.
Hardcoded relative path 'static/js/app.js' vulnerable to same working directory issue; should use absolute path resolution relative to test file.
The parser's handle_data method is not implemented, so <title> content is never captured; self.title remains None even if <title> exists.
The test test_index_html_contains_required_structure asserts parser.title is not None, but due to missing handle_data implementation, it will always fail even with valid <title> tag.

Missing import for pytest fixture usage; TestClient and FastAPI are imported but router is used without verifying it's a FastAPI instance, risking runtime errors if router is not properly initialized.

Test for /items endpoint does not match documented API contract: no /items endpoint is documented in API CONTRACTS, only /api/v1/health is specified. This test may be testing undocumented/unintended behavior.
Test for POST /items does not match documented API contract: no item creation endpoint is documented in API CONTRACTS. This test may be testing undocumented/unintended behavior.
Test for GET /items/{item_id} does not match documented API contract: no item retrieval endpoint is documented in API CONTRACTS. This test may be testing undocumented/unintended behavior.

Test assertion checks for substring '/api/v1/health' in raw JS source, which is fragile and may produce false positives (e.g., in comments, strings, or unrelated code). Should use more precise parsing (e.g., regex with word boundaries or AST-based analysis) to ensure the endpoint is used in actual fetch calls per API contract.

Redundant test: test_app_js_contains_expected_api_endpoints and test_app_js_contains_fetch_calls_with_expected_paths both assert the same condition ('/api/v1/health' in content). This duplication increases maintenance burden and test noise without adding value.

Test does not validate that 'status' value is non-empty or matches expected values (e.g., 'healthy'). The schema only specifies type 'string', but production tests should enforce semantic correctness.

Test assumes static assets are embedded in HTML as literal paths, but modern frontend builds often use hashed filenames (e.g., /static/css/style.abc123.css). This will cause flaky failures in production.

The endpoint '/static/index.html' is likely not the correct path for serving the main dashboard; the dashboard is served at '/dashboard', and static files should be served via configured static middleware, not directly. This test may pass due to misconfiguration or fail in production.

Test file name 'test_static_css_style.css.py' is invalid: pytest will not discover it correctly due to the dot in the filename (Python interprets 'css' as a module name, causing import issues). Should be renamed to 'test_static_css_style.py'.

The assertion logic for CSS variables is flawed: checking for ':root' OR 'var(' is insufficient — a file may contain 'var()' without ':root' (e.g., in custom property usage), but the test incorrectly passes if *either* is present. More importantly, it does not verify actual variable *definitions* (e.g., '--primary-color: ...'). Should require at least one valid CSS custom property definition.
Test uses hardcoded '/health' endpoint, but API contract specifies '/api/v1/health'. This will cause test to fail or test incorrect endpoint.

Test expects response body {'status': 'healthy'}, but API contract only specifies 'status' as a string field without value constraints. Should verify actual response value matches implementation, not assume 'healthy'.

Module-level mutation of 'app' (app.include_router(router)) causes side effects during import, which violates test isolation and can cause unpredictable behavior when tests run in parallel or when modules are imported multiple times.
Test functions directly use a global 'app' instance instead of a fixture, making tests order-dependent and preventing proper cleanup/reset between tests.
Missing /api/v1/health endpoint as required by API contracts; current implementation lacks health check functionality.
read_dashboard() returns raw HTML content without proper content-type headers (should return HTMLResponse or set media_type='text/html')
read_dashboard() returns error dict instead of 404 HTTP status code when index.html is missing, violating REST conventions and API contract expectations.
Missing import for 'Depends' and 'status' from FastAPI; 'status' is needed for proper HTTP status codes in responses.
Missing import for 'sqlite3.Error' to handle database-specific exceptions; generic Exception masking can hide critical issues.

Missing import for 'List' from 'typing' is redundant (already imported), but more critically, 'List' usage in Pydantic models requires 'from typing import List' — current import is correct, but missing 'Sequence' or 'Tuple' for nested lists like path_coordinates.
Missing import for 'Sequence' or 'Tuple' — 'List[List[float]]' should be validated as 'Sequence[Sequence[float]]' for immutability and correctness in type hints.
Incomplete exception handler: the 'except' block is cut off and missing closing parenthesis and raise statement, causing syntax error.
Missing health check endpoint '/api/v1/health' as required by API contracts; no implementation present.
Missing 'from fastapi import status' and using string-based status codes instead of 'status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR' for maintainability.
Missing closing </head> tag before <body> — invalid HTML structure.
Error section uses inline style='display: none;' instead of a class-based approach, violating CSS variable consistency and maintainability.
Footer links lack aria-labels or context; screen readers cannot determine destination purpose (e.g., 'API Docs' vs 'Health JSON').
Incomplete CSS rule: '.text-center' declaration block is missing closing brace and content, causing cascade failure for subsequent rules.
File begins with invalid syntax: triple-quoted string literal (Python-style) and escaped newline characters are not valid JavaScript. This will cause immediate parse failure.
DOM object contains over 80 properties with no initialization or usage logic. This indicates incomplete or placeholder code unsuitable for production.
No actual application logic is present (e.g., no fetch calls, no DOM manipulation, no event handlers). The file fails to fulfill the dashboard's required functionality.

moderate_issues.description: Regex pattern '\bdashboard\b' may match unintended substrings (e.g., 'dashboarding'); consider stricter matching or context-aware validation.
Regex pattern '\bflood\b' may match unintended substrings (e.g., 'flooded'); consider stricter matching or context-aware validation.
Whitespace-removing check for 'fetch(' is fragile and may miss valid invocations (e.g., 'fetch (') or match false positives (e.g., in comments); better to use AST parsing or more precise regex.

The fixture index_html_path uses Path('static/index.html') without absolute path resolution; may fail in different working directory contexts (e.g., CI/CD). Should use Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'static' / 'index.html' or similar.

The test test_index_html_contains_api_endpoints assumes endpoints appear as quoted strings in HTML, but the API contract does not specify how the frontend consumes the endpoint; this test may be overly prescriptive and brittle if implementation changes (e.g., config file, environment variable).

The assertion logic for API endpoints only checks for exact quoted matches, missing cases like template literals (backticks), concatenation, or URL construction patterns (e.g., `API_BASE + '/health'`).
Using MagicMock() without specifying return_value or side_effect may lead to tests that pass but don't validate actual behavior; consider using more specific mocks or patching real clients.
Same as above — generic MagicMock() for Redis client may hide missing method implementations or incorrect usage in production code.

Test_health_endpoint uses hardcoded path '/api/v1/health' in parametrize but the fixture-based client may not reflect actual app setup if router is not mounted at root; consider verifying router path prefix alignment.
test_create_item_validation_error assumes 422 for empty payload, but validation behavior depends on Pydantic model definition; should verify model schema matches expectation.

Error message assertion in test_get_item_endpoint for 404 case is fragile: checks for 'not found' or 'Item not found' in detail, but FastAPI default 404 detail is 'Not Found' (not 'Item not found'), suggesting mismatch between exception handling and expected response.
Test assumes exact JSON response structure without validating against the API contract schema (e.g., missing validation that 'status' is a string, not null or other type).
Test for static files mounts root ('/') but does not verify that the HTML content is valid or matches expected structure; relies on substring match which may be brittle.

Test uses raw file size check (st_size > 0) but does not validate JS syntax or validity. A non-empty file may still contain invalid JS (e.g., syntax errors), leading to false confidence in production readiness.

Test for function/variable definitions uses overly broad pattern matching (e.g., 'const ' could match strings or comments). This risks false positives and does not verify actual exports or callable functions as required by the dashboard's 'status' widget.
Test does not verify that the '/api/v1/health' endpoint is used with 'fetch' (only presence in file), violating the API contract requirement that fetch be used for API calls.
Missing import for response status code validation (e.g., using httpx or explicit status checks). While pytest handles basic assertions, explicit validation improves clarity and maintainability.
Test checks for exact string matches of asset paths without verifying actual file existence or content-type headers, which could mask missing or misconfigured static file handling.

The test for design system properties checks for substrings like 'color' anywhere in the file, which may yield false positives (e.g., in comments or strings). Should use regex or more precise parsing to match actual property declarations.

Basic brace/parentheses balancing checks are insufficient for CSS syntax validation — they ignore nested structures, quoted strings (which may contain braces/parens), and CSS comments. A proper CSS parser (e.g., cssutils) should be used for robust validation.

No handling for file encoding issues — read_text() defaults to UTF-8, but if the CSS file uses a different encoding (e.g., UTF-16 with BOM), it may raise UnicodeDecodeError. Should specify encoding='utf-8' explicitly and handle exceptions.

test_app_includes_router patches api_router but doesn't verify actual inclusion in app.routes — patching is unnecessary and misleading since app creation is not mocked; better to test via client or inspect app.routes directly without patching.
test_health_endpoint unnecessarily patches api_router, which may mask issues with router registration or endpoint registration. Patching should be avoided unless mocking external dependencies.

test_docs_endpoint_exists checks for 'swagger-ui' or 'redoc' in response text, but FastAPI may render docs without those exact substrings (e.g., via custom templates). More robust to check response.status_code == 200 and verify HTML structure or use /openapi.json instead.
Missing type hints for test functions and payload dictionaries reduces maintainability and IDE support.
Test for validation error (422) does not verify the error response structure (e.g., 'detail' field), which is important for API contract validation.
Test for history endpoint does not validate the structure of individual history items (e.g., expected fields like 'timestamp', 'depth'), risking incomplete contract coverage.
STATIC_DIR resolution may be fragile if application is bundled (e.g., PyInstaller) or run from different working directories; Path(__file__) may not resolve as expected in all deployment scenarios.
read_dashboard() reads entire HTML file into memory on each request; for production, consider caching or using FileResponse for better performance.
DEBUG flag derived directly from ENV without validation; could be misleading if ENV is set to non-standard values like 'prod' or 'staging'.
DATABASE_URL default uses SQLite in development, which may cause accidental usage in production if DATABASE_URL is not set; should be validated or raise error in non-dev environments.
API_PORT is cast to int without error handling; if APP_PORT env var is non-numeric, will raise ValueError at import time.
Pydantic model 'SensorData' uses 'datetime' without timezone awareness; ISO format may cause ambiguity in distributed systems.
Pydantic model 'EvacuationRoute' uses 'List[List[float]]' without validation of coordinate structure (e.g., [lon, lat] pairs); should enforce length=2 for each coordinate.
Database connection not closed in case of exception during cursor execution; potential resource leak.
No input sanitization/validation for 'sensor_id' and 'location' beyond min_length; vulnerable to SQL injection if DB_PATH is user-controlled (though unlikely).
No rate limiting or pagination on GET endpoints; may cause performance issues with large datasets.
Timestamp conversion to ISO format before DB storage may lose microsecond precision depending on SQLite schema; should verify schema uses TEXT/REAL for timestamps.
Incomplete exception handler: missing 'raise HTTPException(...)' after the 'except' block, causing runtime syntax error.

Logger level is set to INFO after handler configuration, but the handler inherits the logger's level. Since the logger's level is set after adding the handler, the handler may not respect the intended INFO level in some edge cases (though current order is generally safe, it's better practice to set logger level before adding handlers).
No support for configurable log levels or environment-based verbosity (e.g., DEBUG in dev, INFO in prod), limiting flexibility in production environments.
Google Fonts link uses 'display=swap' but no font-display: swap fallback is declared in CSS, risking FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text).

Status card content lacks semantic structure:
should be

or for better accessibility and semantics.
Live flood data section uses generic 'Fetching real-time sensor data...' — should specify data source (e.g., 'Sensors: 12/15 active') or be more precise per design requirements.
Error section has no role='alert' or aria-live for dynamic error announcements; critical for emergency dashboards.

Missing responsive viewport meta tag handling: no max-width constraint on container for small screens (e.g., padding-left/right may overflow on mobile); consider adding padding-left/right to container or using media queries.
Z-index scale lacks highest-tier values for complex overlays (e.g., modals with dropdowns), risking stacking context issues in production.
Missing focus-visible support: --focus-ring uses :focus but not :focus-visible, which may cause inconsistent focus styling in modern browsers (especially for keyboard vs. mouse users).
DOM object uses magic strings as keys but no corresponding selectors or query logic is implemented to bind them to actual DOM elements.
Excessive and redundant evacuationMap-related properties (e.g., handlers, state flags) suggest over-engineering without clear separation of concerns or modularity.
No input validation, error boundaries, or fallback behavior defined for UI state updates (e.g., statusCard, errorContainer).
